focus: Default-on integration: seam and capability, decision tiers, per-fetch cost, failure modes, risks
ruledOut: Default-on blocking at the decision line

label: The only candidate seam is a PostToolUse matcher for WebFetch|WebSearch; existing hooks prove the advisory additionalContext channel, while blocking capability stays UNKNOWN and must be checked first.

Measured tier composition: 0.25 -> 33 TP + 7 FP; 0.5 -> 31 + 5; 0.75 -> 26 + 0. A block tier with zero false positives existed on this run; advisory at 0.25, block at 0.75 is the policy the data supports, from 3-rerun curves only.

Cost: p50 324ms / p95 388ms per call, ~694 estimated tokens per 5-60-line section; one call per fetched section, ~1s for three-call protocol, ~650ms for the measured two-call early exit; real pages need a byte cap and their own measurement.

Availability is three silent skips plus a retry: PATH, exact version, auth exit 0; exit 4 retries once; drift is only detectable against a stored report, so a hook must log model per call and alert on change.

Risk ledger: FP 9.1% of clean at 0.5 and 12.7% at 0.25; FN 11.4% at 0.5 including reporting-redirection misses; precision passed 3 FPs from kill; payload leaves the machine on real (possibly private) pages; hosted provider behind a pinned version.

Staged plan: capability check, re-measure on real fetch output with label hashes, ship extended lexical floor (9/30) then advisory Jev (review 0.25, block 0.75), log payload/model per call, publish skip behavior.
